es.summary: La alkalosis metabólica es un trastorno del equilibrio ácido‑base caracterizado por pH >7.45 y aumento del HCO₃⁻ en sangre. Se produce por pérdida de ácido o ganancia de bicarbonato.
key_points: pH >7.45 y HCO₃⁻ >26 mEq/L indican alkalosis metabólica.
Compensación respiratoria: hipoventilación para retener CO₂.
Causas comunes: vómitos prolongados, diuréticos de asa, hipopotasemia.
Tratamiento: corregir la causa, reposición de K⁺ y Cl⁻, ácido clorhídrico si es grave.
Complicaciones: arritmias, disminución de perfusión cerebral.

pathophysiology: Pérdida de ácido gástrico (vómitos) reduce H⁺ y aumenta HCO₃⁻.
Uso de diuréticos de asa provoca pérdida de Na⁺, Cl⁻ y K⁺, generando reabsorción de HCO₃⁻.
El aumento de HCO₃⁻ eleva el pH sanguíneo.
El cuerpo intenta compensar mediante hipoventilación para retener CO₂.
risk_factors: Uso de diuréticos de asa (furosemida, bumetanida).
Administración excesiva de bicarbonato o soluciones salinas hipertónicas.
diagnostics: Electrolitos séricos: K⁺ ↓, Cl⁻ ↓, Na⁺ normal o ↑.
Análisis de orina: excreción de H⁺ disminuida.
treatment: Suspender diuréticos de asa o reducir su dosis.
Reposición de potasio con cloruro de potasio (KCl) IV o PO.
Reposición de cloro con solución salina 0.9 % IV.
Acetazolamida para aumentar excreción de bicarbonato en casos graves.
complications: Disminución del flujo cerebral → mareos, síncope.
nursing_care: Monitorear pH, HCO₃⁻, PaCO₂ y electrolitos cada 4‑6 h.
Evaluar signos de hipoventilación y nivel de conciencia.
Administrar KCl y NaCl según prescripción, vigilar irritación venosa.
Registrar ingesta y pérdida de líquidos; mantener balance hídrico.
patient_teaching: Explicar la importancia de no interrumpir tratamientos sin consultar al médico.
Instruir sobre signos de hipopotasemia (calambres, palpitaciones).
Recomendar dieta rica en potasio (plátano, papaya) si es apropiado.
Enseñar técnicas de respiración lenta para evitar hiperventilación.

outcomes: NOC: Mantener electrolitos dentro de rangos normales (K⁺ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L) en 24 h
NOC: Evitar arritmias relacionadas a desequilibrio electrolítico

interventions.action: Monitorear niveles séricos de K⁺, Na⁺ y Cl⁻ cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detectar rápidamente desviaciones y permitir intervención oportuna

interventions.action: Administrar cloruro de potasio IV según orden médica
Evaluar ingesta y pérdidas de líquidos, registrar balance hídrico
interventions.rationale: Identificar fuentes de pérdida de electrolitos

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre alimentos ricos en potasio
interventions.rationale: Facilitar la reposición natural de K⁺

evidenced_by: disminución de la tolerancia al ejercicio
outcomes: NOC: Incrementar la tolerancia a la actividad en 2 niveles de escala de Borg en 48 h
NOC: Mantener nivel de energía reportado ≥7/10 en 3 días

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de actividad y registrar escala de Borg antes y después
interventions.rationale: Establecer línea base y medir progreso

interventions.action: Planificar períodos de descanso cada 10‑15 min durante actividades
Administrar reposición de potasio y cloro según prescripción
interventions.rationale: Corregir causa fisiológica de la intolerancia

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de respiración diafragmática para mejorar ventilación
Coordinar con fisioterapia para ejercicios de bajo impacto

en.summary: Metabolic alkalosis is an acid-base disorder characterized by pH >7.45 and increased HCO₃⁻ in blood. It occurs due to loss of acid or gain of bicarbonate.
key_points: pH >7.45 and HCO₃⁻ >26 mEq/L indicate metabolic alkalosis.
Respiratory compensation: hypoventilation to retain CO₂.
Common causes: prolonged vomiting, loop diuretics, hypokalemia.
Treatment: correct the cause, replace K⁺ and Cl⁻, hydrochloric acid if severe.

pathophysiology: Loss of gastric acid (vomiting) reduces H⁺ and increases HCO₃⁻.
Use of loop diuretics causes loss of Na⁺, Cl⁻ and K⁺, leading to HCO₃⁻ reabsorption.
The increase in HCO₃⁻ raises blood pH.
The body attempts to compensate by hypoventilation to retain CO₂.
risk_factors: Excessive administration of bicarbonate or hypertonic saline solutions.
treatment: Discontinue or reduce loop diuretic dose.
Replace potassium with potassium chloride (KCl) IV or PO.
Acetazolamide to increase bicarbonate excretion in severe cases.
complications: Reduced cerebral blood flow → dizziness, syncope.
nursing_care: Monitor pH, HCO₃⁻, PaCO₂ and electrolytes every 4‑6 h.
Assess for hypoventilation and level of consciousness.
Administer KCl and NaCl per order, monitor for venous irritation.
Record intake and output; maintain fluid balance.
patient_teaching: Explain the importance of not interrupting treatments without consulting the physician.
Instruct on signs of hypokalemia (cramps, palpitations).
Recommend a potassium-rich diet (banana, papaya) if appropriate.
Teach slow breathing techniques to avoid hyperventilation.

outcomes: NOC: Maintain electrolytes within normal ranges (K⁺ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L) within 24 h
NOC: Prevent arrhythmias related to electrolyte imbalance

interventions.action: Monitor serum levels of K⁺, Na⁺ and Cl⁻ every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detect deviations quickly and allow timely intervention

interventions.action: Administer IV potassium chloride as ordered
Assess intake and output, record fluid balance

outcomes: NOC: Increase activity tolerance by 2 levels on the Borg scale within 48 h
NOC: Maintain reported energy level ≥7/10 for 3 days

interventions.action: Assess activity level and record Borg scale before and after
Plan rest periods every 10‑15 min during activities
Administer potassium and chloride replacement as prescribed
Teach diaphragmatic breathing techniques to improve ventilation
Coordinate with physical therapy for low-impact exercises
interventions.rationale: Improve muscle strength without overloading the system

summary.1.quote: Identifying and treating the root cause, either hydrogen ion loss or bicarbonate ion gain, is essential because the risk of mortality increases as pH increases (Tinawi, 2021).

key_points.1.quote: A nurse may first suspect that a patient has metabolic alkalosis because they may have a decreased respiratory rate; this is the result of the lungs trying to retain additional CO 2 to increase the acidity of the blood and resolve the alkalosis.

key_points.4.quote: If not corrected, it can lead to decreased myocardial contractility, arrhythmias, decreased cerebral blood flow, confusion, and even death.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Gastrointestinal loss of hydrogen ions can occur as a result of vomiting or gastric suctioning.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: This is because gastric secretions have high levels of hydrogen ions: as acid is lost, the pH level of the bloodstream increases.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Metabolic alkalosis has a variety of causes, including prolonged vomiting and nasogastric suctioning.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: For example, loop and thiazide diuretics can create a secondary hyperaldosteronism that leads to excess urine excretion of hydrogen.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: A nurse may first suspect that a patient has metabolic alkalosis because they may have a decreased respiratory rate; this is the result of the lungs trying to retain additional CO 2 to increase the acidity of the blood and resolve the alkalosis.

sections.complications.2.quote: Extended or severe alkalemia results in a relative hypocalcemia, as ionized calcium tends to bind more readily to proteins in an alkalotic environment (Hopkins et al., 2022).

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: When a patient demonstrates signs of potential hypercapnia, the nurse should assess airway, breathing, and circulation.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: The main nursing interventions for patients with acid-base imbalances include closely monitoring respiratory and neurological status for deviations from baseline that would indicate worsening of the imbalance monitoring and recording accurate intake and output monitoring and treating the specific acid-base imbalance monitoring vital signs
